name: net-b3-clock-interpolation
title: Netcode B3: clock sync and snapshot interpolation of remote entities
issue: Design: C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/netcode-runtime-design.md (N1-N15 ACCEPTED): read the whole document, the sections for this stage and the stage table row, then the MERGED code: n2net (transports, SecureTransport, channels, the network simulator and its tests), N2Server, B1 (NetworkObject, world/server/client classes, fingerprint) and B2 (field replication: .Replicated(), codecs, delta vs acked baseline, NetworkTransform) in engine/src/network, A2 (simulation clock, fixed tick, StepTicks, TickOptions), and the existing network docs page. Follow the security rules of the design (bounded counts and sizes before allocation, rate limits, authority checks, no client-controlled allocation). The web build must still compile (n2net core is compiled for web; native sockets are not). Nothing builds locally: re-read every edit twice and trace identifiers. SCOPE (stage B3 only): (1) client/server clock synchronisation over the existing secure channel (ping/pong style samples with the server tick and a monotonic client clock; filtered offset and RTT estimate using the best-of-N or a median filter, drift handling, never jumps backwards; bounded rates, malformed input rejected; estimates exposed to C++ and Lua as server time/tick, RTT, jitter); (2) snapshot interpolation of remote entities: the client buffers received NetworkTransform states per object with their server ticks, renders remote objects at (estimated server time - interpolation delay) interpolating position/scale linearly and rotation by slerp, with a configurable delay (default from settings: a few snapshot intervals), extrapolation limited and clamped when a snapshot is late, teleport flag respected (no interpolation across a teleport), buffer bounded (no unbounded growth under a flood or long stalls), out-of-order and duplicate snapshots handled; the locally controlled object (owner/prediction) is NOT interpolated (that is B6): provide the hook; (3) tests on the network simulator (latency, jitter, loss, reorder): clock estimate converges and stays within bound; interpolated position is smooth (bounded second difference) under jitter; teleport; late snapshot extrapolation clamp; buffer bounds; deterministic given a seeded simulator; (4) docs: the clock/interpolation section of the netcode docs and scripting-lua.html for the Lua accessors, true against the code. Nothing builds locally for the engine; CI (12 checks) is the test; expect fix rounds; re-read every edit twice (CMake/YAML/C++ syntax); NEVER call a stateful function (RNG etc.) twice in one argument list or operator expression (unspecified evaluation order); NEVER run taskkill or kill other processes; verify every docs sentence against the CODE; no attribution lines on commits or PRs (no Co-Authored-By, no Generated-with footer); GitHub only via the wrapper; before your final push merge origin/master into the branch if it moved; your FINAL message must be a real report (PR number, head sha, what you did, deviations), never a single word.
acceptance: Clock sync converges, never goes backwards, bounded rates; exposed to C++ and Lua
Snapshot interpolation with delay, bounded extrapolation, teleport, bounded buffers
Simulator tests incl. jitter/loss/reorder; docs true; CI green
notes: Reviewer: monotonic clock estimator, no division by zero or NaN at startup (first samples), buffer and rate bounds, tick wraparound handling (u32 ticks), slerp of non-normalised or NaN rotations, interpolation never applied to the locally controlled object, compile-level correctness, web build.
